premiums.name: MJP Q4 (Main Japanese Port)
premiums.src: COMPILED SATURDAY 07-NOVEMBER-2026 (LME BOARD ON THE FRIDAY 06-NOVEMBER OFFICIAL, THE LAST TRADING SESSION; NO RING ON SATURDAY). PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY, AND THIS PANEL CARRIES EACH ROW AT ITS OWN LAST PUBLIC ASSESSMENT DATE. CIF JAPAN SPOT REFRESHED THIS RUN TO SMM'S 09-OCTOBER ASSESSMENT: CIF Japan MJP spot $230/t (warehouse-warrant $269/t; FCA South Korea $223/t, CIF South Korea $216/t, CIF Thailand P1020A $249/t), down from the $370/t last public spot carried since Q3. SMM's read is that overseas premiums are 'near a floor' with the outlook 'less bearish', though a stronger rebound needs better downstream orders. The prior $370/t mark and the new $230/t mark are not guaranteed to share one assessor, so the size of the step is indicative. EVERY OTHER ROW IS CARRIED UNCHANGED at its own last public assessment. SMM also cites the US Midwest duty-paid premium at 105 US cents/lb (about $2,315/t) on 09-October - context from a different source, not substituted into the US rows. CONTEXT FROM A DIFFERENT ASSESSOR, NOT MIXED INTO ANY ROW: AL Circle (06-October) reports CRU's Asia CIF premium at $202/t and Q4 MJP offers down to $245-260/t from $325/t in early September, against the $395/t Q3 benchmark; earlier SMM reporting (30-September) had Rio Tinto at $280/t and South32 at $265/t. Q4 SETTLEMENT NOW PUBLIC: Reuters (07-October) reported that some Japanese buyers agreed Q4 premiums of $255/t with global producers including Rio Tinto and South32, down 35% from $395/t in Q3 and below initial offers of $310-325/t; talks with other buyers were ongoing. This page first recorded it on 11-October. THE TARIFF DECOMPOSITION IS REFRESHED DAILY BY DESIGN: on a re-verified Section 232 rate of 50% on aluminium articles applied to full customs value, the tariff leg of the US duty-paid premium is 0.50 times the 06-November official cash of $3,117.00, or $1,558.50, DOWN $9.00 against the 04-November figure used previously. Against a US Midwest duty-paid premium of $2,403/t that leaves a residual market leg of $844.50, so 64.9% of the US duty-paid premium is policy arithmetic rather than market. This page does NOT fabricate freight, financing or tightness splits for any premium row. SOURCE DISAGREEMENT FLAGGED 17-OCTOBER: SMM's 16-October overseas-market analysis describes Q4 MJP negotiations as slow, with the two sides 'diverging significantly' on price; this is consistent with Reuters' 07-October report that $255/t was agreed with SOME buyers while talks with others continued. The $255/t settlement is retained; no new figure was located. Source: https://news.metal.com/newscontent/104162844-smm-analysis-overseas-primary-aluminum-market-remains-weak-offer-prices-under-pressure-across-major-markets

macro_events: THE EXCHANGE RANG ON MONDAY AND THE CONFIRMATION TEST RESOLVED HALF-WAY. On the 28-September official aluminium cash fell $5.50 to $3,248.50 and three-month $15.00 to $3,252.00, but the contango narrowed a second consecutive ring to $3.50. Visible stock was unchanged at 241,375 t, so the pre-registered bull upgrade (narrowing plus a draw) was not triggered.

THE BOARD ROLLED TO THE MONDAY 28-SEPTEMBER OFFICIAL. Tuesday's official prints at 13:20 London, after this page compiles, so 28-September is the latest settled session. Completeness verified: the cache-busted English and German overviews agree on all six metals, stock lines and FX fixings; the aluminium and nickel per-metal daily tables show 28-September as the newest row; and all five stock lines reconcile against the 25-September levels. The next official is Tuesday 29-September at 13:20 London.

CHINESE CUSTOMS DATA PUBLISHED FRIDAY CUT THE EX-CHINA PULL ARGUMENT FROM BOTH ENDS, AND IT IS THE MOST SUBSTANTIVE NEW FUNDAMENTAL INFORMATION IN THIS WINDOW. August primary aluminium imports fell 14.65% year on year to 185,500 tonnes, with Russia supplying 96% of them; January-August imports were 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. On the same day, August aluminium extrusion exports printed a 2026 high of 92,500 tonnes, up 9.7% year on year, with September guided lower at 85,000-92,000 tonnes on a narrowing China-to-overseas price spread. Less Chinese buying of ex-China primary and more Chinese semis in third markets both work against the ex-China tightness case, whatever the stated structural cause.

THE RATE PATH WORSENED AGAIN AND THE WHOLE LME COMPLEX FELT IT. The US ten-year is near 5.24%, close to its highest since 2002, with roughly 70% market-implied odds of an October Fed hike; the dollar index is near 101.28 and the LME euro fixing fell to 1.1375 from 1.1403. Copper fell 1.33% and zinc 2.54% on cash on 28-September; aluminium's front tightened regardless.

THE ENERGY AND CURRENCY LEGS BOTH EASED. European gas TTF fell 4.02% to EUR 71.93/MWh, the largest single-session fall of this window and a direct improvement in the economics of the European smelting capacity currently guided to restart; Brent slipped 0.56% to $106.01; the dollar index fell 0.32% to 100.966 and the LME euro fixing rose 0.30% to 1.14030, ending two sessions of dollar strength. Cheaper European power is bearish for price through supply and supportive for European converter margins - the two effects are opposite and are stated separately rather than netted.
lme_commentary: A ROUND TRIP ON THE WEEK, WITH THE STRUCTURE STILL TIGHTENING. Two officials were added this run. Thursday 05-November lifted three-month $23.50 to $3,097.50 - a settled close above 3,077 and the 3,084.00 rebound high - with cash $3,160.00 and a $62.50 backwardation. Friday 06-November then gave it all back: cash $3,117.00 (-$43.00) and three-month $3,050.00 (-$47.50), back below 3,061.5 on the weekly close, though still $25.50 above the 3,024.50 bear trigger. Under the pre-registered rules the bull gained five points on Thursday and returned them on Friday, so weights end the week at 15/45/40. Structure went the other way: the backwardation widened to $67.00, the widest since mid-September, visible stock fell 875 t to a new low of 227,600 t, and cancelled warrants rose to 17,375 t on 05-November (AL Circle) - spread and price moved in OPPOSITE directions on Friday. The Friday drop was broad - zinc three-month -2.79%, copper -1.78%, aluminium -1.53%, lead -0.63%, nickel flat - as the dollar index rose about 0.7% to 102.28 after October US payrolls of 165,000 beat a 65,000 forecast, and Brent and European gas extended steep weekly losses on hopes of a US-Iran diplomatic track (Trading Economics, 06-November). On the week three-month is down $30.00 (from $3,080.00 on 30-October). October's official means were cash $3,061.11 and three-month $3,057.64; three-month now sits $7.64 below its October mean.

alumina_notes: THE ALUMINA PANEL REFRESHED PROPERLY THIS RUN FOR THE FIRST TIME IN A MONTH, AND THE MESSAGE IS QUIET-BUT-SOFTENING. SMM's 24-September weekly index prints at 2,671.59 yuan/tonne, down 2.35 yuan/tonne or 0.09% week on week, with all five regional quotes flat week on week - Shandong 2,640-2,710, Henan 2,680-2,740, Shanxi 2,670-2,730, Guangxi 2,580-2,630, Guizhou 2,720-2,780. This replaces a 25-August mark of 2,600 yuan/tonne that this page had been carrying for a month, and the difference between the two is a month of drift, not a session's move. PUBLISHED ON THE SAME DAY: China's weekly alumina operating rate rose 0.23 percentage points to 76.89%, on 119.62 million tonnes a year of installed metallurgical-grade capacity and 91.97 million tonnes of operating capacity. MORE ALUMINA BEING MADE AT A PRICE THAT IS NOT MOVING IS A SOFT SIGNAL FOR ALUMINA AND THEREFORE A SUPPORTIVE ONE FOR SMELTER MARGINS, SINCE ALUMINA IS ROUGHLY A THIRD OF A SMELTER'S CASH COST AND IT TAKES ABOUT TWO TONNES OF IT TO MAKE ONE TONNE OF METAL. It is also a reminder that the cost-side relief on this page is coming from alumina while the cost-side pressure is coming from energy, which rose again today. The dollar-denominated rows - FOB East Australia, the exchange-settled alumina close and the futures reference - carry no newer dated print into this window and are held at their true assessment dates. The freshest hard FOB East Australia datum remains the 18-September SMM-reported trade at $354/mt for October shipment.
net_read: NET: NEUTRAL - PRICE SOFT, STRUCTURE TIGHT. earnings.headline: Q2 FY27: Vedanta group revenue INR 258.12bn (+57% y/y), EBITDA INR 99.38bn (+106%), PAT INR 62.02bn (+151%), net debt/EBITDA 0.1x. earnings.readthrough: AN INTEGRATED, LOW-COST PRODUCER IS STILL CONVERTING THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO RECORD MARGIN: a 46% aluminium EBITDA margin on record volume, with alumina self-supply rising 37%. Read-through: unlike Hydro's and Alcoa's alumina legs, integrated producers that consume their own alumina capture the low alumina price as a cost benefit. (The source's group-margin figure appears internally inconsistent and is not used.)

earnings.headline: Q3-2026: revenue $2.64bn (from $2.17bn, about +22%); adjusted EBITDA $276m (from $235m, about +17%); net income $119m (from $88m); shipments 368 kt, slightly lower y/y. 2026 guidance RAISED to adjusted EBITDA of $1.03-1.06bn excluding non-cash metal price lag and free cash flow above $300m. Metal price lag was unfavourable in Q3 (amount not disclosed in the source).
earnings.readthrough: CONVERSION MARGIN IS HOLDING ON LOWER VOLUME: revenue rose faster than EBITDA because metal prices pass through, while shipments edged lower - so the guidance raise reflects pricing and cost rather than volume. The fall from Q2's $439m to $276m is largely the reversal of metal-price-lag gains, which is why guidance is stated excluding lag. Generic read for primary metal: downstream demand is stable, not accelerating.

earnings.eps: n/d (the company reports on Adjusted EBITDA rather than headline EPS): Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA $439m, a record, of which $129m is non-cash metal price lag, so $310m excluding lag; H1-2026 $798m including $226m of lag; FY2026 guidance $980m-$1.020bn excluding lag with free cash flow above $300m; leverage 1.8x
earnings.headline: BACKFILLED INTO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A FULL FOUR-QUARTER SOURCED HISTORY. Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter.
earnings.readthrough: THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

earnings.eps: n/d (final dividend for FY26 recommended at Re 1.00/share, Rs 183.66 crore)
earnings.headline: Q1 FY27 net profit Rs 2,002.38 crore against Rs 1,063.86 crore a year earlier, up 88%, on revenue from operations of Rs 5,302.38 crore, up 39.01%, and profit before tax of Rs 2,649.66 crore, up 87.33%. The company reported its highest-ever Q1 bauxite excavation at 19.52 lakh tonnes and its highest-ever Q1 calcined alumina production at 5.77 lakh tonnes. Added to this board and to the earnings-history panel this run as the designated progressive backfill.
earnings.readthrough: NALCO IS THE MOST FULLY INTEGRATED PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL - IT MINES ITS OWN BAUXITE, REFINES ITS OWN ALUMINA AND SMELTS - AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THIS PRINT IS USEFUL RATHER THAN JUST GOOD. A company that buys none of its alumina nearly doubling profit on record volumes tells you where margin is sitting in the chain: with whoever owns the alumina. Read directly against Chalco, the largest alumina producer in the world, whose Q2-2026 attributable profit fell 26.2% year on year in a quarter when the LME cash average was above $3,200 - the difference between the two is not the metal price, which both received, but scale, cost position and product mix. IT ALSO CUTS AGAINST THE ALUMINA-COST-SHOCK RISK THIS BOARD CARRIES: an integrated refiner posting record Q1 alumina output at 5.77 lakh tonnes is evidence of alumina availability rather than scarcity, and it sits on the same side of the argument as the alumina-to-aluminium ratio near 10.7-11.3%, well below the historical norm. THE HONEST QUALIFICATION: NALCO's exposure is predominantly Indian and its cost base is domestic coal-fired, so it is a weak read on seaborne alumina tightness, which is where this board locates the risk. Public listed-company disclosure, carried to read the cycle only.

earnings.headline: STRONGEST QUARTER OF THE YEAR AT THE DOWNSTREAM END OF THE CHAIN. Fourth-quarter FY26 revenue rose 25.2% year-on-year to MYR 204.8 million (USD 50.8 million) from MYR 163.5 million (USD 40.5 million), on higher sales volumes in the group's extrusion and fabrication segment; the company reports its strongest quarterly revenue and profit of the financial year, with the headline putting quarterly profit up about 200% to roughly USD 4.5 million. The result funds a MYR 100 million (USD 24.8 million) expansion plan and a diversification away from its core solar-sector business. FIGURES ARE TAKEN FROM THE PUBLIC REPORT AS PUBLISHED; the full profit-and-loss detail below the revenue line was truncated in the public summary and nothing is inferred to fill it.
earnings.readthrough: A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. SMM's 24-August daily describes Chinese downstream processing operating rates as under pressure with pre-peak-season stockpiling absent, and Chinese billet inventory is at a five-year seasonal high. A South-East Asian extruder posting 25% revenue growth and its best quarter of the year says the weakness is not uniform across Asia - which is consistent with the trade-flow story on this board, where South-East Asia is being consolidated as the major supplementary scrap source by the UAE export ban and EU tariff increase. IT IS A SMALL COMPANY AND ONE QUARTER, SO IT IS WEIGHTED ACCORDINGLY: it is evidence that extrusion demand outside China is holding, not evidence that the global peak season has arrived.

earnings.headline: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%).
earnings.readthrough: THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.headline: H1-2026 unaudited interim results: revenue RMB 87.5bn (+8.0% y/y), gross profit RMB 27.5bn (+32.3%), profit for the period RMB 19.1bn (+41.0%), net profit attributable RMB 17.2bn (+39.2%), basic EPS RMB 1.734 (+32.0%).
earnings.readthrough: THE READ-THROUGH IS ABOUT COST, NOT PROFIT. Gross profit rose 32.3% on revenue up only 8.0% because cost of sales DECLINED outright - the cleanest public confirmation this reporting season that the alumina price collapse has reached the integrated Chinese cost curve. For the metal itself this cuts both ways and the bearish leg deserves equal billing: the world's largest producer earning record margins at $3,200-3,300/t has no economic reason to restrain output, and a lower cost curve lowers the price floor at which supply discipline would ever appear. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.headline: SWUNG BACK TO PROFIT ON THE PRICE CYCLE, WITH TEXTBOOK OPERATING LEVERAGE. Unaudited H1-2026 interim results, approved at an 18-August board meeting and filed 19-August: ADJUSTED EBITDA UP 64.4% TO US$1.23bn from US$748m; revenue up 10.9% to US$8.338bn from US$7.52bn; adjusted net profit US$196m against a US$194m loss a year earlier. Total sales cost rose 3.3% to US$6.31bn, attributed to higher energy costs.
earnings.readthrough: REVENUE UP A TENTH AGAINST EBITDA UP NEARLY TWO-THIRDS IS THE SAME OPERATING-LEVERAGE SIGNATURE EVERY OTHER PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL HAS REPORTED FOR THE FIRST HALF, and it confirms the pattern extends beyond Western and Gulf smelters. The cost line is the part worth noting rather than the profit line: sales cost rose only 3.3% while revenue rose 10.9%, so the margin expansion came from price rather than from cost deflation, and the company specifically attributed what cost inflation there was to ENERGY. That is consistent with the power and carbon risk carried on the input basket. The half captured aluminium reaching four-year highs before the retreat now visible on this board, so it is a backward-looking confirmation of the cycle rather than a forward signal.

earnings.headline: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%.
earnings.readthrough: THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.headline: MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY WITH A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE. Adjusted net profit Dh2.46bn, up 34% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. The company estimates around Dh1.5bn of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah, most of it in 2026, and guided cast metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 with the smelter at 25% of its reduction cells as of 26-Aug-2026 (315 of 1,262).
earnings.readthrough: THE COMPOSITION IS A PUBLIC CONFIRMATION OF THE MARGIN STRUCTURE THIS BOARD HAS DESCRIBED ALL CYCLE. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. The read-across to the alumina panel is direct - if Alunorte's 50% rate ends up lifting seaborne alumina, this is the margin that compresses first across the Gulf fleet.

earnings.headline: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning.
earnings.readthrough: THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

earnings.headline: Q2-2026 BEAT AND A HIGHER Q3 GUIDE: adjusted EBITDA attributable $326.9m against $315-335m guidance and $231.4m in Q1; net sales $752.1m (Q1 $649.2m); shipments 130,632 t (Q1 122,865 t); net income attributable $249.3m; diluted EPS $2.39; adjusted EPS $2.46. Q3-2026 guidance $325-345m. Liquidity $784.9m with cash $343.4m; cash exceeded total debt as of end-July after a $94.3m 2025 45X refund was received. Q2 adjustments included $61.3m for an Iceland equipment failure (net of tax) and $10.7m of Mt. Holly expansion cost.
earnings.readthrough: THE PUREST US AND SECTION-232 READ IN THE PEER SET, AND IT CONFIRMS THAT THE 2026 PRICE AND TARIFF STRUCTURE IS CONVERTING TO CASH. Adjusted EBITDA rose 41% sequentially on a 6.3% increase in shipments, which is operating leverage on price and premium rather than on volume. The last 90 Mt. Holly pots have been restarted, taking the plant to full capacity for the first time since 2015, and Grundartangi Line 2 is near full - so the volume base steps up again into Q3, which is why the guide moved higher despite Q2 already beating. THE COST-SIDE SIGNAL MATTERS FOR THE WHOLE BOARD: management again cited UNFAVOURABLE RAW-MATERIAL PRICE REALISATION as the principal EBITDA headwind, the second consecutive quarter it has done so. That is the same message the input basket carries - a firming alumina and bauxite leg partly offsetting a falling energy leg - and it is the reason a rising LME does not translate one-for-one into producer margin.

earnings.headline: BACK-FILLED INTO THE PER-COMPANY HISTORY PANEL THIS RUN WITH FOUR SOURCED QUARTERS OF ADJUSTED EBITDA. Q1 FY27 (three months to 30-June-2026): net income $164m, up 71% year on year; ADJUSTED EBITDA $516m, UP 24% year on year; adjusted EBITDA per tonne shipped $563, up 30% year on year; net sales $5.8bn. The prior three quarters were $459m in Q4 FY26 (down 3% y/y, $544/t), $348m in Q3 FY26 (down 5% y/y, $430/t) and $422m in Q2 FY26 (down 9% y/y, $448/t) - all three depressed by the Oswego fires of September and November 2025 and by tariff headwinds.
earnings.readthrough: THE FOUR-QUARTER SERIES IS THE POINT AND IT IS WHY THIS COMPANY WAS CHOSEN FOR THIS RUN'S BACKFILL: it is the cleanest public evidence available of how a downstream converter recovers from an operational shock, and of what the 2026 premium environment has been worth to the downstream. Adjusted EBITDA fell for three consecutive quarters - $422m, $348m, $459m - and then stepped up 12.4% sequentially and 24% year on year to $516m in the June quarter. THE PER-TONNE LINE IS THE MORE INFORMATIVE OF THE TWO because it strips shipment volume out: $448, $430, $544, $563. That is a 31% improvement in unit conversion economics across four quarters in a business whose metal cost is passed through. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE IS AS IMPORTANT AS WHAT IT DOES: a converter's EBITDA per tonne rising through a period of record US premiums is consistent with the premium being captured downstream, but Novelis does not publish a split between recovered metal-price spread, recycling spread and true conversion pricing, so this page does not claim one. THE GENERIC READ-ACROSS IS THAT THE DOWNSTREAM SIDE OF THE CHAIN ENTERED THE SECOND HALF OF 2026 WITH MOMENTUM, which is consistent with Constellium and Kaiser on the same panel and with the stable $727.50 Rotterdam billet conversion spread on the premium panel.

earnings.headline: Q2-2026 profit attributable to equity holders BHD 64.9m (US$172.5m), +164% y/y; Q2 EBITDA US$295m; EPS 46 fils. H1 profit BHD 140.2m (US$372.8m), +228% y/y; EPS 99 fils. OPERATIONALLY THE WEAKEST PRINT IN THE PEER SET: Q2 net finished production 155,469 t, DOWN 61% y/y, and sales volume 280,799 t, -32% y/y, with Lines 1, 2 and 3 still under controlled shutdown on regional tensions and raw-material availability. Value-added product was 195,891 t, 70% of shipments.
earnings.readthrough: THE SHARPEST ILLUSTRATION ON THIS BOARD OF WHAT THE 2026 MARKET IS ACTUALLY REWARDING: a producer can lose 61% of its output year-on-year and still nearly triple half-year profit, because average LME rose 46% y/y to $3,576/t in Q2. It also quantifies the supply loss the deficit rests on - Alba's own read put the Q2 global deficit at 934,000 t including China and 626,000 t excluding it, with global supply contracting about 1% mainly on Middle East disruption. Management explicitly framed the curtailments as preserving flexibility for a swift recovery when conditions improve, which is the restart option the bearish case depends on. Separately Alba is progressing its US$2.2bn acquisition of Aluminium Dunkerque, about 300,000 t/y and the largest EU smelter.

earnings.headline: Q3-2026: revenue $3.704bn (-7% q/q from $3.966bn); net income attributable $483m, $1.81/share; ADJUSTED EPS $1.82 against $2.12 in Q2 - a BEAT against the ~$1.54 consensus cited by Investing.com while revenue missed (~$3.78bn expected). Alumina production +11% to 2.467 Mt (Pinjarra stability); aluminium production +2% to 649 kt (Alumar restart complete); total aluminium shipments -5% to 693 kt. Realised aluminium $4,527/t (Q2 $4,752/t); third-party alumina $353/t (Q2 $334/t). FY2026 production and shipment guidance reaffirmed.
earnings.readthrough: THE FIRST Q3 PRODUCER PRINT SHOWS THE PEAK IS BEHIND THE AVERAGE REALISED PRICE: a ~5% q/q fall in realised aluminium and a 7% revenue drop, offset by better costs and a higher alumina price. Q4 guidance flags about $30m of higher raw-material costs and maintenance in the aluminium segment and about $30m higher alumina costs - consistent with an industry where the metal price is easing faster than input costs. The South32 aluminium chain acquisition (shareholder-approved 15-October) is guided to close in H1-2027. Generic public read-through, not advice.

earnings.headline: Q3-2026: adjusted EBITDA NOK 9,089m against NOK 8,923m in Q2 and NOK 5,996m in Q3-2025; Aluminium Metal adjusted EBITDA NOK 7,031m (Q3-2025 NOK 2,732m); Bauxite & Alumina NOK 283m (from NOK 1,290m); Energy NOK 411m (from NOK 828m). Reported net income NOK 5,263m, adjusted net income NOK 4,372m, adjusted EPS NOK 2.3 (Q3-2025 NOK 1.0). Free cash flow NOK 1.4bn, reduced by higher working capital tied to higher metal prices; adjusted net debt NOK 21.9bn (NOK 22.8bn last quarter). Capex guidance cut to about NOK 12.5bn from NOK 13.5bn; Slovalco's first restart phase targets 75,000 t/y by end-February 2027. Shares fell about 7% on the day (Investing.com).
earnings.readthrough: THE SMELTER LEG IS STILL EARNING ON PRICE, THE ALUMINA LEG IS NOT. Aluminium Metal EBITDA more than doubled year on year on higher all-in metal prices despite lower volumes and higher energy and carbon costs, while Bauxite & Alumina fell nearly 80% on lower alumina prices, LNG sourcing costs at Alunorte (about $85m in Q3, $90-110m guided for Q4 per management) and BRL effects. Hydro describes the ex-China alumina market as oversupplied and ex-China primary demand as declining, with Middle East tension keeping aluminium prices elevated - the same split as Alcoa's Q3: metal margin intact, alumina margin compressing, cash absorbed by working capital.

earnings.headline: Net profit RS 5,629cr, +216% YoY (consolidated PAT reported at RS 6,597cr, +205%, on some feeds - consolidation basis differs); revenue RS 21,393cr (+46% YoY); EBITDA RS 10,299cr vs RS 8,352cr in Q4 FY26 (+23% q/q), margin 48.1% vs 43.7%; interim dividend RS 8/share; record output 632 kt (+5% y/y) with record value-added 389 kt (+14%).
earnings.readthrough: The cleanest India read on the 2026 regime: a low-cost integrated producer converting the price/premium environment into a near-50% EBITDA margin, with volume records on top. Confirms the pattern set by Alcoa, Hydro, Rio and South32 - the Hormuz-era price structure is flowing straight through to producer P&Ls, and value-added mix is expanding, not shrinking, into the squeeze.

earnings.headline: Net profit $200.3m (+316% YoY); EPS 53 fils; sales −17% on Gulf supply-chain disruption.
earnings.readthrough: LME averaged $3,195/t (+22% YoY) drove profit surge; volumes hit by regional conflict; ~19% capacity in controlled shutdown — restart path improves post-truce.

earnings.headline: Net profit SAR 2.18bn (+13% y/y, +33% q/q); revenue SAR 10.9bn (+16% y/y, +24% q/q); gross profit SAR 3.39bn (-4%) and operating profit SAR 2.36bn (-8%).
earnings.readthrough: A clean example of the split running through this whole peer season: the top line and the bottom line rose on higher commodity prices across all business units and higher aluminium and gold sales volumes, while GROSS and OPERATING profit FELL on input and logistics cost inflation - here concentrated in phosphate (sulphur, freight) rather than in the aluminium chain. Net profit was additionally helped by higher finance income, lower finance costs and a larger share of equity-accounted profits, so the headline overstates the operating improvement. The generic read for the aluminium market is the same one Century and Hindalco delivered from opposite ends of the integration spectrum: a rising metal price is not converting one-for-one into margin wherever the input leg is bought rather than owned.

earnings.headline: Group revenue $31.0bn (+15%); underlying EBITDA $14.8bn (+28%); free cash flow +75%; dividend raised. ALUMINIUM segment EBITDA +31%. Primary aluminium 1,676 kt (flat), alumina 4,040 kt (+8%), bauxite 28.5 Mt (-7%).
earnings.readthrough: UPDATE 17-OCTOBER (Q3-2026 operations review, 14-October, production only - no new earnings figures): primary aluminium 842 kt (-2% y/y), alumina 2,071 kt (+10% y/y), 2026 aluminium guidance 3.25-3.45 Mt unchanged; average Midwest duty-paid premium $2,420/t on about 32% of Q3 volumes. The H1-2026 earnings figures in this row are unchanged. Reported this morning and the freshest producer datapoint in this report. A 31% rise in aluminium EBITDA on flat volumes is a pure price-and-premium effect, confirming that the current regime is generating exceptional upstream margins. Two supply items matter for the forward view: Yarwun output will be CUT 40% from October 2026 (~1.2 Mt/y) on tailings constraints, extending life to 2035, and AP60 Arvida ($1.5bn, +160 kt/y) completes commissioning by end-2026.

earnings.headline: RECORD QUARTER, AND THE THIRD IN A ROW. Press Metal Aluminium reported net profit of MYR 624.5m for the quarter ended 31-March-2026, UP 35.2% year-on-year from MYR 461.77m, on revenue of MYR 4.1bn (+5.2%). The company attributed the result to stronger aluminium prices, higher sales volumes and LOWER INPUT COSTS - the same three forces visible in every other producer on this panel. ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN as the tenth company in the earnings_history series. THE PERIOD IS DELIBERATELY OLDER THAN THE REST OF THE PANEL AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: Press Metal's Q2-2026 result had not published publicly at this compile and is expected in late August. Nothing has been estimated to fill the gap.
earnings.readthrough: WHY IT WAS WORTH ADDING: Press Metal is the largest primary aluminium producer in South-East Asia and the panel was otherwise weighted to Western, Indian, Gulf and Chinese producers. It is a hydro-powered, non-Chinese, non-Gulf smelter - which makes it the cleanest available control on the question of whether the margin expansion running through this panel is genuinely driven by the metal price and the cheap alumina leg, or by region-specific factors like Section 232 protection or Gulf supply disruption. A 35% profit increase at a producer with no exposure to either strongly supports the former. ITS Q2 RESULT IN LATE AUGUST IS THE MORE INTERESTING DATAPOINT, because it will cover the quarter in which alumina fell to roughly 10.7% of the metal price.

earnings.headline: ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A PRIMARY-SOURCED HISTORY TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM SEC FILINGS RATHER THAN FROM COVERAGE. Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million.
earnings.readthrough: THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

Hydro's per-company history was rolled to Q3-26 (Q3-25 dropped). NO NEW COMPANY WAS BACK-FILLED INTO THE PER-COMPANY HISTORY THIS RUN; gaps stay gaps. Both Q3 producer prints so far (Alcoa, Hydro) show the same split: smelting margin intact on price, alumina margin compressing. ALCOA OPENED THE Q3-2026 PRODUCER SEASON ON 15-OCTOBER (refreshed this run): adjusted EPS $1.82 beat the ~$1.54 consensus on better costs and higher alumina output and prices, while revenue fell 7% q/q as the realised aluminium price eased to $4,527/t. Alcoa's per-company history was rolled to Q3-26 (Q3-25 dropped). NO NEW COMPANY WAS BACK-FILLED INTO THE PER-COMPANY HISTORY THIS RUN; gaps stay gaps. Next in the season: Norsk Hydro and Rio Tinto later in October. SEASON DATE CONFIRMED: Alcoa reports Q3-2026 on Thursday 15-October after the New York close (Alcoa via Medianet), opening the producer reporting season. Vedanta's Q2 FY27 production release (03-October) showed record aluminium of 649,000 t and alumina of 895,000 t; financials follow later. PEER EARNINGS ARE A LULL AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN PADDED. No peer result printed into this window; the freshest item on the panel remains Constellium's Q2 and H1-2026 on 29-July, and the Q3-2026 reporting season does not open until mid-October. NO NEW COMPANY WAS BACK-FILLED INTO THE PER-COMPANY HISTORY PANEL THIS RUN, AND THE REASON IS PUBLISHED RATHER THAN LEFT BLANK. The twenty companies already carried cover the priority list in full - Maaden (1211), Chalco, Hindalco, Vedanta, Alba and Rio Tinto half-years are all present. The candidate this run was an additional Rio Tinto half-year point for H1-2024; the public release located does not disclose Aluminium product-group underlying EBITDA in the material available, and this panel's rule is that gaps stay gaps and nothing is interpolated or estimated. The point is therefore NOT added. EVERY FIGURE IN THIS PANEL IS AN EXACT PUBLICLY REPORTED NUMBER TAKEN FROM A COMPANY RELEASE, A REGULATORY FILING OR PUBLISHED PRESS. Where a company reports on a half-year or fiscal-year basis the unit says so; where a series has fewer than four points that is because fewer than four are publicly verifiable on a consistent basis, not because the series was trimmed. THE PANEL'S CENTRAL READ IS UNCHANGED AND WORTH RESTATING BECAUSE THE PRICE MOVED TODAY: the 2026 earnings cycle across producers and converters is overwhelmingly a PRICE and ALUMINA-RATIO story rather than a volume story, which is exactly why the alumina-to-metal ratio at 11.13% is the number to watch for when that cycle turns.
commercial: COMMERCIAL READ - GENERIC AND PUBLIC. FIRST, PROMPT PREMIUM UP, PRICE DOWN: a $67.00 backwardation on 06-November, wider than $62.50 even as cash fell $43.00 and three-month $47.50 - a sixth print above the $15.00 reversal condition, so nearby metal is valued clearly over forward metal and there is no carry reward for deferring purchases; the outright price closed the week $27.00 below 3,077 after briefly settling above it on Thursday. SECOND, ASIAN PREMIUMS ARE RESETTING LOWER: the Q4 MJP settled at $255/t for some Japanese buyers (Reuters, 07-October), down 35% from $395/t in Q3, and CRU's Asia CIF spot is lower still at $202/t. THIRD, THE TARIFF ARITHMETIC MOVED WITH THE METAL: on a verified 50% Section 232 rate, the tariff leg of the US Midwest duty-paid premium is $1,558.50 on 06-November cash, 64.9% of the $2,403/t premium. bottom_line: BOTTOM LINE: the week ended with LME aluminium three-month at $3,050.00 on the Friday 06-November official, down $47.50 on the day and $30.00 on the week, after Thursday briefly settled above 3,077 at $3,097.50. The backwardation nevertheless widened to $67.00 and visible stock fell to a new low of 227,600 t, so prompt tightness and outright price are diverging. Weights end at 15% bull / 45% base / 40% bear: the bull gained five points on Thursday's pre-registered close above 3,077 and returned them on Friday's settled close below 3,061.5. Re-crediting the bull needs another settled close above 3,077 with the backwardation beyond $15.00; a close below 3,024.50, or a contango beyond $24.50, adds bear weight. balance.label: UPDATE 02-OCTOBER: Macquarie revised its 2026 deficit to 820,000 t from 940,000 t and forecasts a 410,000 t surplus in 2027, citing the faster EGA Al Taweelah restart (via Discovery Alert). Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND THE 11-SEPTEMBER DATA SHARPENS THE CENTRAL PUZZLE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT: global primary production was reported down 1.7% year on year at 6.16 million tonnes and GCC output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000 - a genuine, large supply loss. YET China's August exports were 626,000 tonnes, taking January-August to 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year, and dated commentary describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE with Asian premiums collapsing toward a $280-290 Q4 consensus. A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.

THE TIGHTENING SIDE, DATED: visible LME stock near multi-decade lows at 241,375 tonnes, about 9,840 tonnes below the August mean; a 0.50% weekly draw; Chinese pre-holiday destocking of 118,000 tonnes in two weeks, the steepest on the 2020-2026 record; an alumina-to-metal ratio of 11.13% against a decade norm of 15-17%, which is what has underwritten producer earnings all year; a Gulf supply picture still contested in public with Qatalum curtailed and no published restart date; and, this run, a curve that tightened $11.50 and a weekly close that held the 3,261 retracement. THE LOOSENING SIDE, EQUALLY DATED: the US ten-year Treasury yield at 5.214%, a further multi-year high; Chinese August primary imports down 14.65% year on year with Russia at 96% of supply, and extrusion exports at a 2026 high of 92,500 tonnes, both reducing the pull on ex-China units; publicly recovering ex-China operating capacity, with Alba the largest single tranche in the public record this cycle and Century, Slovalco and Magnitude 7 all guided; a European gas reference down 4.02%, which improves the economics of the European capacity guided to return; Chinese spot metal still clearing at discounts on 24-September; and Chinese alumina refining running at only 76.89% of 119.62 Mt/y, so no feedstock constraint is available to squeeze the cost curve. WHY IT IS THE MODAL CASE: the range has absorbed a nineteen-year-high yield, a record Chinese destock, a multi-week decline and now a sharp one-session reversal without breaking in either direction. That is the definition of a market where neither side can finish the job.

WHAT THE CASE STILL RESTS ON, AND IT REMAINS THE STRONGEST STRUCTURAL ARGUMENT ON THE PAGE: the US ten-year Treasury yield at 5.214%, a further multi-year high, raising the cost of carrying inventory and the discount rate on every project; Chinese August primary aluminium imports DOWN 14.65% year on year at 185,500 tonnes with Russia at 96% of supply, and August extrusion exports at a 2026 HIGH of 92,500 tonnes - both meaning the ex-China market faces less Chinese buying and more Chinese semis; ex-China operating capacity recovering in public, with a European gas reference down 4.02% making the guided European restarts more likely rather than less; Chinese spot metal clearing at repeated discounts on 24-September with spot circulation described as shifting to oversupply; Chinese alumina capacity running at 76.89%, so a quarter of refining capacity is idle and available to cap the cost curve; and a cash price still $30.84 below its own September-to-date mean. WHAT WOULD RESTORE THE WEIGHT, PRE-REGISTERED SO IT CAN BE CHECKED: a weekly close beneath 3,261 on three-month, or a daily settlement beneath 3,183 which is the hard invalidation of the constructive daily count, or a return of the contango to beyond $24.50. None of those is met today.

risks.risk: THE CONTANGO RISK IS CUT FROM UP TO DOWN, AND THE CUT IS EARNED ON THE LARGEST SINGLE-SESSION SPREAD MOVE OF THIS SEQUENCE. The cash-to-three-month spread NARROWED $11.50 to a $13.00 CONTANGO on the 25-September official from $24.50, which was the widest reading of the sequence - the first narrowing in five rings, and almost half the contango removed in one ring. The eight-session sequence reads backwardations of $21.00 and $18.50, then $3.00, then contangos of $10.50, $22.00, $20.00, $24.50 and now $13.00. THE CHINESE TRADE PULL IS RAISED TO UP AS A NEW NAMED RISK, AND IT IS THE MOST SUBSTANTIVE NEW FUNDAMENTAL INFORMATION IN THIS WINDOW. Customs data reported 25-September show China's August primary aluminium imports DOWN 14.65% year on year at 185,500 tonnes, with Russia supplying 178,150 tonnes or 96% of the total; net imports 163,600 tonnes, down 14.67%; January-August 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. On the same day August extrusion exports printed a 2026 HIGH of 92,500 tonnes, up 9.7% year on year, with September guided lower at 85,000-92,000 tonnes on a narrowing price spread. The stated cause of the import fall is structural - capacity at the 45-million-tonne ceiling, resilient end-use demand, inventory drawn down through semis exports - but the effect on the ex-China balance is identical whatever the cause: less Chinese competition for ex-China primary units and more Chinese semis competing with Western fabricators. THIS DIRECTLY WEAKENS THE LOAD-BEARING ASSUMPTION OF THE EX-CHINA DEFICIT CASE. UPDATE 20-OCTOBER: China's September unwrought primary imports fell 30.3% y/y to about 172 kt (SMM) while output ran a record Q3 at about 46.7 Mt annualised (Reuters via Finimize). Trend held at UP.

THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM OVERHANG IS HELD AT UP AND THE EVIDENCE GOT BROADER RATHER THAN DEEPER. SMM's 24-September South China review records transactions concentrated at a 250-290 yuan/tonne premium over the SHFE 2610 contract but quotes lowered repeatedly through the session, most deals concluded at actual DISCOUNTS, phased stockpiling complete, procurement slowing and spot circulation shifting to oversupply, with cashing out before the holiday the dominant driver. To that this run adds a structural leg: August extrusion exports at a 2026 high of 92,500 tonnes with September guided lower on a narrowing China-to-overseas price spread that compresses exporter margins, and processing trade gaining share over ordinary trade. A physical market clearing at discounts while exporting record volumes on thinning margins is a demand picture that depends on price, not on need. UPDATE 28-SEPTEMBER: SMM's Monday print shows 6063 billet inventory RISING 5,500 tonnes from Thursday to 154,500 tonnes and the ingot draw slowing to 4,000 tonnes, with central-China metal at a 20-70 yuan/tonne discount to SHFE and limited downstream stockpiling - the overhang is starting to show in inventory, not only in commentary. UPDATE 20-OCTOBER: record Q3 primary output (11.84 Mt, +2.2% y/y) above the 45 Mt cap pace supports the overhang read. Trend held at UP.

THE COST FLOOR IS CUT FROM UP TO DOWN, AND IT IS THE MOST ECONOMICALLY MEANINGFUL MACRO MOVE ON THE BOARD TODAY. European gas TTF fell 4.02% to EUR 71.93/MWh on the 25-September reference session, the largest single-session fall of this window, and Brent slipped 0.56% to $106.01 after the previous session's 3.90% jump. Power is roughly 30-40% of smelter cash cost and is the largest single line after alumina, so a falling energy complex lowers the marginal cost floor and therefore the price floor. IT ALSO WORKS THE OTHER WAY AND BOTH ARE STATED: cheaper European gas directly improves the economics of the European smelting capacity publicly guided to return, which is a supply risk rather than a price support. The arrow is down because the floor fell; the supply consequence is carried on the ex-China restart row. EU CARBON-BORDER COST IS A SLOW, STRUCTURAL RISK TO EUROPEAN DELIVERED PRICE AND IT IS HELD AT FLAT. No new dated instrument or rate change printed into this window. The 6% EU import duty plus the carbon border adjustment mechanism remains a structural floor under European delivered prices and a persistent disadvantage for high-carbon origins, which is why the European duty-unpaid premium and the Rotterdam duty-paid billet premium behave differently from the Japanese benchmark. It is carried here as a structural risk rather than a live one precisely because it moves on legislative rather than market timescales.

CHINA'S NATIONAL DAY HOLIDAY AND THE POST-HOLIDAY REBUILD TEST - THE CLEANEST FORWARD TEST ON THE PAGE, BECAUSE IT IS THE ONE WHERE THIS PAGE HAS NAMED THE MECHANISM IN ADVANCE. The 118,000-tonne two-week destock to 24-September is attributed by its own source to pre-holiday stockpiling and a widening spot-futures spread. Both drivers reverse by design once the holiday ends: stockpiled metal is consumed rather than bought, and the spread normalises. If Chinese inventory rebuilds sharply in the first two weeks of October, the single strongest bullish number on this page will have been a calendar effect; if it does not rebuild, the destock was demand and the deficit case strengthens materially. That is a genuine binary and it resolves in mid-October. THE SIX-YEAR RECORD SETS THE YARDSTICK (SMM via AL Circle, 26-September): across 2020-2025 ingot inventory rose 4% to 17.3% over the holiday week and total inventory 6.9% to 21.2%. A rebuild at the bottom of that band would confirm the pre-holiday destock as demand; a rebuild at or above the top would mark it as timing.

Today is the strongest available evidence for the second half of that sentence. The rate remains a real and persistent headwind; it is not the determinant of the aluminium front.

THE MOST SUBSTANTIVE NEW FUNDAMENTAL INFORMATION IN THIS WINDOW IS BEARISH AND IT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A DAY'S NOISE. Chinese customs data published 25-September show August primary aluminium imports DOWN 14.65% year on year at 185,500 tonnes, with Russia supplying 96% of them, and January-August imports down 3.41% at 1.66 million tonnes. On the same day, August extrusion exports printed a 2026 HIGH of 92,500 tonnes, up 9.7% year on year, with September guided lower on a narrowing price spread. China at the 45-million-tonne ceiling is buying less ex-China primary and shipping more semis into third markets. Both work against the ex-China tightness case that a substantial part of this year's price level rests on, and the stated structural cause does not change the arithmetic.

THE LEVEL ARGUMENT STILL CUTS AGAINST THE DAY AND IT IS PUBLISHED RATHER THAN OMITTED. Cash at $3,254.00 is $30.84 BELOW the September-to-date official cash mean of $3,284.84 and only $4.37 above the August mean of $3,249.63. The month has been a decline and one ring does not reverse it. The published curve-reversal condition - a return to backwardation beyond $15.00 on a settled official - remains UNMET, and a $13.00 contango is still a market that charges to wait. The honest description of today is a meaningful improvement inside an unbroken range, not a turn.

THE COST BASKET GAVE MORE INFORMATION THAN USUAL AND IT IS MIXED. Four new dated marks printed: aluminium fluoride mainstream 11,500-12,500 yuan/tonne with the low end unchanged and the top widening; cryolite 8,300-9,000 with the low end up 3.75%; oxygen-blown #553 silicon 9,400-9,500, up 100 yuan week on week with the rise in the upper half of the range; and magnesium DOWN, with the Fugu 99.90% midpoint at 15,800 against 16,200 on 07-September, cutting that row's trend flag to down. Where a range widened at the top without moving at the bottom, the series is held flat and the fact is stated. Meanwhile European gas fell 4.02% and Brent slipped 0.56%, so the cost floor fell - which lowers the price floor and simultaneously improves the economics of the European capacity guided to restart.

THE ALUMINA RATIO IMPROVED FOR SMELTERS WITHOUT ANY ALUMINA PRICE CHANGING, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS. Alumina at $363.60/t against the 25-September three-month of $3,267.00 is 11.13%, down from 11.18%, against a decade norm of 15-17%. That is a margin event delivered entirely by the revenue line. The structural picture is unchanged: a firm seaborne market attributed to Middle East shipping frictions, a flat Chinese index at 2,671.59 yuan/tonne, and Chinese refining running at only 76.89% of 119.62 Mt/y - a quarter of capacity idle and available if price ever asks. That is not a structural alumina shortage, and the risk to producer margin remains a rising Chinese index rather than a firm seaborne one.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE VIEW, PRE-REGISTERED SO IT CAN BE CHECKED AGAINST NEXT WEEK'S BOARD. TO UPGRADE FURTHER: a second consecutive narrowing of the contango on Monday's official PLUS a visible stock draw - either alone is insufficient, because Friday's weakness was precisely that the curve moved without inventory. TO REVERSE: a weekly close beneath 3,261 on three-month, a daily settlement beneath 3,183 which is the hard invalidation of the constructive daily count, or a return of the contango to beyond $24.50. TO CONFIRM THE CONSTRUCTIVE DAILY COUNT OUTRIGHT: a daily settlement above 3,374, now $107.00 overhead on three-month against $121.50 on the prior session - the first session in four in which that objective has moved closer rather than further away.

premium_explainer: PREMIUMS ARE WHAT A BUYER PAYS OVER THE EXCHANGE PRICE TO GET PHYSICAL METAL DELIVERED TO A PARTICULAR PLACE, AND THEY ARE THE PART OF THE DELIVERED PRICE THAT THE EXCHANGE DOES NOT SET. They are assessed by price-reporting agencies from reported transactions on defined periodic cycles - quarterly for the Japanese benchmark, weekly or twice-weekly for most spot assessments - which is why this panel carries each row at its own assessment date instead of pretending to a daily figure. Each row is carried at its own last public assessment date; the CIF Japan spot row uses SMM's 09-October mark. THREE THINGS DRIVE A PREMIUM: the cost of physically moving and financing metal to that location; how hard it is to get metal there right now; and policy - duties, tariffs and carbon costs that apply at the border. THE POLICY COMPONENT IS THE ONLY ONE THAT CAN BE CALCULATED RATHER THAN ASSESSED, AND THIS PAGE CALCULATES IT SEPARATELY SO THE TWO ARE NEVER CONFUSED. At a verified 50% Section 232 rate on full customs value, the tariff leg of the US duty-paid premium is $1,627.00 against cash of $3,254.00, which is 67.7% of the $2,403/t US duty-paid premium. The remaining $776.00 is the market leg. When cash moves, the tariff leg moves with it mechanically and the market leg absorbs the difference - today cash rose $26.00, the tariff leg rose $13.00 and the market leg fell $13.00 without any physical market having changed. THE EXCHANGE CURVE IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ ON THE IMMEDIACY COMPONENT, AND IT IMPROVED FOR THE SELLER TODAY. A contango means the market charges to defer metal, which weakens a physical premium; a backwardation means it pays for metal now, which strengthens one. The contango narrowed $11.50 to $13.00 from $24.50 on the 25-September official, so the buyer's structural argument going into the Q4 Japanese settlement is weaker this morning than it was on the prior session.
premium_outlook: UPDATE 12-OCTOBER: SPOT HAS SLIPPED BENEATH THE NEW BENCHMARK. SMM (09-October) assesses CIF Japan MJP spot at $230/t against the $255/t Q4 settlement, and calls overseas premiums 'near a floor' as selling pressure eases. Watch whether remaining Japanese buyers settle at $255/t or below, and where Q1-2027 offers open from late November. UPDATE 11-OCTOBER: THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE QUARTERLY PREMIUM HAS SETTLED AT $255/T, DOWN 35% FROM THE $395/T Q3 RECORD (Reuters, 07-October; some buyers, with talks continuing for others). The chart's pending band is replaced by the settled value. The settlement landed at the low end of the offer range and above CRU's $202/t Asia CIF spot assessment, so spot still sits beneath the benchmark: the next test is whether Q1-2027 talks open lower again. Drivers cited publicly are recovering Gulf output and rising Indonesian shipments. UPDATE 01-OCTOBER: THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE QUARTERLY SETTLEMENT IS STILL PENDING AT THE START OF THE QUARTER IT PRICES. SMM reports (30-September) that a major producer cut its Q4 MJP offer to $280/t from $310/t and that the market expects the final settlement BELOW $280/t, with Korean and Thai spot demand described as subdued to very weak. The pending band carried on the chart remains the publicly reported OFFER range of $280-310/t with v set to null; on the SMM read the eventual settlement may print beneath that band, which would be a fall of more than 29% from the Q3 record of $395/t. PRIOR: THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE QUARTERLY SETTLEMENT IS THE LARGEST SINGLE DATED EVENT LEFT ON THIS PAGE AND IT IS NOW INSIDE TWO WEEKS. The pending range carried here is $280-310/t against the settled Q3 record of $395/t, which would be a fall of 22% to 29%. That range is a publicly reported negotiating range, not a settlement, and it is carried with v set to null so the chart shows a pending band rather than a false print. WHAT MOVED THE ARGUMENT THIS RUN, AND IT MOVED AGAINST THE BUYER: the cash-to-three-month contango NARROWED $11.50 to $13.00 from the $24.50 that was the widest reading of this sequence. A buyer arguing for a deep cut leans on a curve that charges to defer metal; that argument is close to half as strong this morning as it was on the prior session. WHAT STILL FAVOURS THE BUYER: the last public Chinese spot review, dated 24-September, records metal clearing at repeated discounts with quotes lowered through the session; ex-China operating capacity is publicly recovering, with Alba's restart the largest single tranche in the public record this cycle and Century, Slovalco and Magnitude 7 all guided; European gas fell 4.02% on the 25-September reference session, improving the economics of the European capacity guided to return; and Friday's Chinese customs data show August primary imports down 14.65% year on year, which means less Chinese competition for ex-China units. WHAT FAVOURS THE SELLER BESIDES THE CURVE: Chinese pre-holiday destocking of 118,000 tonnes across two weeks is the steepest on SMM's 2020-2026 record; visible LME stock is near multi-decade lows and about 9,840 tonnes below the August mean; and the Gulf supply picture remains contested in public with Qatalum still curtailed and no published restart date. THIS PAGE TAKES NO VIEW ON WHERE IT SETTLES AND WILL PUBLISH THE FIGURE WHEN IT IS PUBLIC. The honest read is that the evidence on both sides is dated, public and genuinely mixed, and that the single most negotiation-relevant number - the exchange curve - moved against the buyer this week.
alumina_explainer: ALUMINA IS THE FEEDSTOCK: it takes roughly two tonnes of alumina to make one tonne of aluminium, so the alumina price is the single largest raw-material line in a smelter's cost stack - about 34% of Chinese full cost on public estimates. A smelter's margin is therefore driven as much by what alumina costs as by what aluminium sells for.

THE RATIO MATTERS MORE THAN THE LEVEL. Alumina at $363.60/t against an aluminium three-month of $3,267.00 is a ratio of 11.13%, against a decade norm of 15-17%. Alumina is therefore still historically CHEAP relative to metal. The ratio fell from 11.18% on the prior session and the reason is worth stating precisely: the metal rose 0.45% and no alumina price changed. When a ratio moves because its denominator moved, that is a margin event for smelters, not an alumina event.

THE DIVERGENCE THIS PAGE HAS TRACKED FOR SEVERAL RUNS IS UNCHANGED AND STILL THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THIS PANEL: Chinese alumina has been drifting sideways to lower while ex-China alumina has been firmer. The SMM index at 2,671.59 yuan/tonne for 24-September is essentially flat, and FOB East Australia at $354.00/t for 18-September sits well above the Q2-2026 average of $307.40/t. Two independent series, one Chinese and one seaborne, pointing different ways is a stronger observation than either alone.

THE CAUSE IS LOGISTICS RATHER THAN A SHORTAGE OF REFINING CAPACITY, WHICH IS WHY IT SITS ALONGSIDE THE HORMUZ ROW. The ex-China firmness has been publicly attributed to Middle East transport problems lifting demand for bagged alumina and for alternative origins, not to any shortfall in installed refining capacity.

SUPPLY ITSELF IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT AND THAT IS STATED SO THE DIVERGENCE IS NOT OVER-READ. China's national weekly alumina operating rate is 76.89% on 119.62 Mt/y of capacity, so there is very substantial idle refining capacity available to respond to any sustained price signal. A seaborne market that is firm because of shipping frictions, sitting on top of a refining industry running at roughly three-quarters of capacity, is not a structural alumina shortage.

WHAT TO WATCH: whether the Chinese index resumes falling while the seaborne price holds. If it does, ex-China smelters keep a cost advantage relative to Chinese peers that is unusual in this cycle; if the Chinese index turns up, the cheapest leg of the global cost curve rises and the margin story narrows for everybody. SMM publishes the index weekly on Thursdays, so the next print is due 01-October.

Mysteel (16-October) reports a major Shandong-based smelter raised its benchmark prebaked-anode purchase price by Yuan 400/t from September to Yuan 6,130/t (cash; Yuan 6,147/t by acceptance) - above Yuan 6,000 for the first time in 44 months on a feedstock rally - against an estimated production cost of about Yuan 6,167.5/t. BASIS OF THE HISTORY SERIES: the monthly Shandong benchmark tender, cash price, Yuan/t (one smelter's benchmark, not a national average); October appended at 6,130, consistent with the carried September mark of 5,730 plus the reported Yuan 400 increase. Nothing is interpolated or estimated. Source: Mysteel - China prebaked anode exceeds Yuan 6,000 on feedstock rally (16-Oct-2026) https://www.mysteel.net/analysis/5144811-china-prebaked-anode-exceeds-yuan-6-000-on-feedstock-rally-

That is bearish for price through supply and supportive for European converter margins; the two effects are opposite and are stated separately rather than netted.

logistics.name: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.val: CONSTRAINED AND CONTESTED. At least three tankers reported attacked transiting the strait this week; US weighing a third carrier group; crude flows largely recovered; no US-Iran agreement
logistics.note: REVIEWED SATURDAY 10-OCTOBER-2026. Trading Economics' Brent coverage (09-October) says the US-Iran conflict continues to strain shipping: tankers are tied up in ship-to-ship transfers outside the Strait of Hormuz, freight rates are at record highs and eleven tankers were attacked in the Strait in the week ending 04-October; President Trump said the US would not strike Iran again before the midterm elections. No container or bulk transit count is published because tracker figures remain disputed. Arrow stays UP pending a public, verifiable normalisation signal. PRIOR: REVIEWED WEDNESDAY 30-SEPTEMBER-2026. Public reporting on 29-September records the US rejecting Iran's seven-day Hormuz reopening plan, new US sanctions on 10 suppliers to Iran's military, and Tehran awaiting a formal US response to its ceasefire proposal; the Strait remains closed. Middle East crude exports reached 12.8 million b/d, the highest since February, but largely via ship-to-ship transfers and pipeline bypasses that do not serve Gulf aluminium exports. No transit count is published because tracker figures remain disputed. Arrow stays UP. PRIOR: REVIEWED TUESDAY 29-SEPTEMBER-2026. Public reporting on 28-September records indirect US-Iran talks resuming through mediators in New York, with the Strait of Hormuz still closed to commercial shipping; Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline resumed after drone-strike repairs, with flows reported near 3.5 million b/d, offering a partial bypass for crude but not for Gulf aluminium exports. Transit counts remain disputed between trackers and outlets, so no transit figure is published. Arrow stays UP until a dated, verifiable reopening step. PRIOR: REVIEWED MONDAY 28-SEPTEMBER-2026. On Saturday 26-September the US President publicly rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap - release of frozen funds, lifting of oil sanctions and an end to the naval blockade within four to five days, with the Strait reopened and negotiations under way by day seven - calling it not acceptable. He told reporters he expects talks to resume in the coming week; separately, US officials were reported as signalling a renewed bombing campaign after the November midterms. Iran's foreign minister said Tehran will not back down on its conditions and awaits mediators' formal feedback. Public tracking (straits.live, 27-September) classifies the Strait as closed to commercial traffic on day 210, with a pre-crisis baseline of about 85 transits a day; some outlets report sizeable US-escorted crude movements, so transit counts are DISPUTED and none is used as a figure here. TREAT THESE AS REPORTED DIPLOMATIC STATEMENTS, NOT SETTLED OUTCOMES. WHY THE ARROW GOES FROM FLAT BACK TO UP: last week's cut to flat rested on a visible negotiation; its latest proposal was publicly rejected and a post-midterm escalation path was reported. Second-order effects stand: regional disruption withdraws tonnage from the global pool and reprices freight on lanes that never touch the Strait.

logistics.name: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.val: DETERIORATED SHARPLY - Houthi forces hold at least five islands and effectively control the strait; transits down to single digits
logistics.note: REVIEWED SATURDAY 10-OCTOBER-2026 (no newer public transit count located; earlier note carried): Trading Economics' Monday Brent commentary (https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/brent-crude-oil) cites Saudi-backed military operations against Houthi forces in Yemen and Houthi control of the Bab el-Mandeb strait as a live market concern. No public transit count newer than the prior reading was located, so none is published. Arrow stays UP. PRIOR: REVIEWED WEDNESDAY 23-SEPTEMBER-2026. THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL NEW PUBLIC INFORMATION THIS RUN IS DIPLOMATIC RATHER THAN OPERATIONAL, AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS. SMM's 23-September summary records that on 22-September US President Trump, speaking at the 81st UN General Assembly, reiterated that the United States would reach an agreement with Iran AFTER THE NOVEMBER MIDTERM ELECTIONS; that Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi met US envoy Witkoff in New York and Trump described a three-hour meeting with the Iranian delegation as very productive with another to be arranged; and that Iran has publicly set CONDITIONS for reopening the Strait of Hormuz - immediate lifting of the maritime blockade, immediate unfreezing of all Iranian assets, and an end to the war on all regional fronts. READ THIS CAREFULLY RATHER THAN OPTIMISTICALLY. A negotiation is now visibly under way, which is the first genuine de-escalation signal of this cycle. But the publicly stated US timetable puts any agreement AFTER November, and Iran's stated conditions are maximalist. The transit constraint is therefore still in force today and is not publicly guided to clear inside this quarter. TREAT THESE AS REPORTED DIPLOMATIC STATEMENTS, NOT AS SETTLED OUTCOMES.

premium_drivers.t: The Q4 Japanese premium has settled 35% lower, at $255/t
premium_drivers.d: SETTLED: Reuters (07-October) reported that some Japanese buyers agreed to pay $255/t over LME cash for October-December shipments, down 35% from $395/t in Q3 and below producers' initial offers of $310-325/t; producers named in the talks included Rio Tinto and South32, and talks with other buyers were ongoing. A Japanese trading-house source cited recovering Middle East output after the March attacks on Gulf smelters and rising Indonesian shipments. Negotiations ran longer than usual because of a wide gap between the two sides. The settlement sits inside the $245-260/t offer range AL Circle reported on 06-October, and above CRU's $202/t Asia CIF assessment. WHY IT MATTERS: the quarterly MJP is the reference for much Asian physical business, so the regional premium level resets about $140/t lower for the quarter.
src: Reuters via LSE.co.uk - Some Japanese aluminium buyers agree to pay Q4 premiums of $255/t, 35% lower than Q3 (07-Oct-2026)

premium_drivers.t: Spot premiums have fallen below the new quarterly benchmark - but sellers' pressure is easing
premium_drivers.d: SMM's 09-October assessment puts CIF Japan MJP spot at $230/t, $25 beneath the $255/t Q4 quarterly settlement, with Korea at $216-223/t and Thailand at $249/t. SMM concludes the outlook for overseas premiums 'has become less bearish' and premiums may stabilise or recover modestly near term, but a stronger rebound needs clearer improvement in downstream orders and restocking. WHY IT MATTERS: with spot below the quarterly benchmark, remaining Japanese buyers have little reason to settle above $255/t, and the Q1-2027 talks start from a lower spot base.
src: SMM - Overseas primary aluminum premiums near a floor as selling pressure eases (09-Oct-2026)

premium_drivers.t: Chinese primary imports fell 14.65% year on year in August, which means less Chinese competition for ex-China metal
premium_drivers.d: Public customs data reported on 25-September show China's August primary aluminium imports at 185,500 tonnes, DOWN 14.65% year on year and up just 0.16% month on month, with Russia supplying 178,150 tonnes or 96% of the total and Australia (2,920 t), Indonesia (2,180 t) and Malaysia (1,800 t) accounting for almost all of the remainder. Net imports were 163,600 tonnes, down 14.67% year on year. January-August imports were 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. THE STATED CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN DEMAND-LED: domestic capacity is at the 45-million-tonne policy ceiling, end-use demand from grid investment, electric vehicles and photovoltaic mounting is described as resilient, and inventory is being drawn down through semis exports rather than primary imports. WHY IT MATTERS FOR PREMIUMS EVEN SO: a premium is set by competition for units at a location. China importing 14.65% less primary metal, and 96% of what it does import arriving from a single discounted-origin supplier, means the marginal ex-China unit faces less Chinese competition - which works against premiums in Japan, Europe and the United States regardless of why Chinese buying fell.
src: AL Circle - China Aug aluminium imports down 14.7% year on year, Russia accounts for 96% of supply (25-September-2026)

premium_drivers.t: Chinese semis exports hit a 2026 high, which pressures converter margins in exactly the markets where premiums are assessed
premium_drivers.d: Public data reported on 25-September show China's August aluminium extrusion exports at 92,500 tonnes, the highest monthly figure of 2026, up 9.7% year on year from 84,300 tonnes and 3.0% month on month from 89,800 tonnes, taking January-August to 629,600 tonnes, up 8.7%. South-East Asia took 26,500 tonnes or 28.6% and was the only region with both the largest volume and double-digit growth; Africa took 18,800 tonnes and Latin America 14,400. SEPTEMBER IS GUIDED LOWER at 85,000-92,000 tonnes because the China-to-overseas price spread has narrowed, compressing margins on independent order-taking; the share of processing trade rose while ordinary trade fell, which the source reads as marginal weakening in price-driven independent orders. THE PREMIUM READ IS SPECIFIC: extrusions compete with locally converted metal in third markets. More Chinese semis arriving in South-East Asia, Africa and Latin America pressures the converter margins that ultimately support regional ingot premiums, even though the same exports support Chinese domestic ingot demand. The two effects are opposite and are stated separately rather than netted.
src: AL Circle - China's August aluminium extrusion exports hit a YTD high; pullback expected in September amid narrowing price spread (25-September-2026)

points: WHAT MOVED: two officials were added. Thursday 05-November: three-month $3,097.50 (+$23.50), cash $3,160.00. Friday 06-November: three-month $3,050.00 (-$47.50, -1.53%), cash $3,117.00 (-$43.00); down $30.00 on the week. No ring on Saturday.

WHY: Friday's sell-off was broad (zinc -2.8%, copper -1.8%, aluminium -1.5%) as October US payrolls of 165,000 beat a 65,000 forecast and the dollar index rose about 0.7% to 102.28; Brent (down more than 12.5% on the week) and European gas (two-week low) kept falling on US-Iran diplomacy hopes, lowering the smelter cost floor (Trading Economics).

THE DIVERGENCE: prompt LME metal keeps tightening - a $67.00 backwardation (widest since mid-September), stock down to 227,600 t, cancelled warrants up to 17,375 t (AL Circle) - while the outright price weakens. Scenario weights moved to 20/45/35 on Thursday and back to 15/45/40 on Friday under the published rules.

WHAT TO WATCH: Monday's official versus $3,042-3,024.50 support and $3,077 resistance; whether the backwardation stays above $15; Hormuz (a fatal tanker attack reported 06-November; Iranian mine claims unconfirmed); first Q1-2027 Japanese premium offers (none public yet).

forward.basis: LME official prices via Westmetall. Baseline = LME 3-month official (a traded market price). Range = random-walk cone from realized volatility. Driver score = 3 transparent rules, hit rate measured on history.
forward.source: London Metal Exchange official settlements via Westmetall (https://www.westmetall.com/en/markdaten.php?action=table&field=LME_Al_cash)

drivers.name: Curve carry (cash − 3M)
drivers.rule: Backwardation (cash above 3M) = prompt physical tightness = bullish; contango = bearish.

drivers.name: Inventory trend (13-week)
drivers.rule: LME stock falling more than 2% over 13 weeks = tightening = bullish; rising >2% = bearish.

drivers.name: Momentum (3M vs 20-week average)
drivers.rule: Price above its 20-week average = uptrend = bullish; below = bearish.

backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 35.1% directional hit rate against a 65.5% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 0.6% versus 6.51% after 'loosening' readings. They are therefore published as a read on CURRENT market condition only — not as a price forecast. The forward baseline and probability range above are the forward-looking view.
backtest.caveat: Measured on overlapping 13-week windows of weekly LME data (111 observations, 2024-05-24 to 2026-08-07). Overlapping windows overstate significance and the sample spans a single, largely rising market — evidence in either direction is weak.

THE LIMIT, STATED: a spot gas reference is not a smelter's contracted power cost, which is bilateral and confidential. This row tracks the public proxy and says so.

Customs data reported 25-September show China's AUGUST PRIMARY ALUMINIUM IMPORTS DOWN 14.65% YEAR ON YEAR AT 185,500 TONNES, with Russia supplying 178,150 tonnes or 96% of the total; net imports 163,600 tonnes, down 14.67% year on year; January-August imports 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%.
