THE STATED CAUSE OF THE IMPORT FALL IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN DEMAND-LED - domestic capacity at the 45-million-tonne policy ceiling, resilient end-use demand from grid investment, electric vehicles and photovoltaic mounting, and inventory drawn down through semis exports rather than primary imports. FIRST, THE INBOUND CORRIDOR: China's August primary aluminium imports fell 14.65% year on year to 185,500 tonnes, with Russia supplying 178,150 tonnes or 96% of the total and Australia, Indonesia and Malaysia accounting for almost all of the rest. January-August imports were 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. A single origin at 96% is a concentration worth recording in its own right, and a 14.65% fall means less Chinese competition for ex-China units. SECOND, THE OUTBOUND SEMIS CORRIDOR: August extrusion exports hit a 2026 high of 92,500 tonnes, up 9.7% year on year, with South-East Asia at 26,500 tonnes or 28.6%, Africa at 18,800 and Latin America at 14,400 - and September guided lower at 85,000-92,000 tonnes on a narrowing China-to-overseas price spread. THE HORMUZ AND RED SEA ROWS ARE UNCHANGED: nothing operational printed into this window, the 07-September negotiating track remains the last dated development, and nothing has been signed. The Canada-United States row is unchanged with the rate re-verified. The Indonesia row is unchanged. NOTHING HERE HAS BEEN ROLLED FORWARD AS IF NEW; each corridor carries its own last sourced development.

flows.impact: Rising - and the newest public data put the outbound semis corridor at a 2026 high
flows.note: REVISED THIS RUN ON NEW PUBLIC CUSTOMS DATA. August aluminium extrusion exports printed a 2026 HIGH of 92,500 tonnes, up 9.7% year on year from 84,300 and 3.0% month on month from 89,800, taking January-August to 629,600 tonnes, up 8.7%. South-East Asia took 26,500 tonnes or 28.6% and was the only region with both the largest volume and double-digit growth; Africa took 18,800 tonnes and Latin America 14,400. SEPTEMBER IS GUIDED LOWER AT 85,000-92,000 TONNES because the China-to-overseas price spread has narrowed, compressing margins on independent order-taking; processing trade gained share while ordinary trade lost it, which the source reads as marginal weakening in price-driven independent orders. THE CORRIDOR READ: semi-finished exports remain the principal mechanism by which Chinese metal reaches shortage markets without primary metal crossing a border, and it is running at its 2026 peak. That relieves physical tightness in Western markets while pressuring Western fabricator margins - the same trade does both, and this page states both rather than netting them. The earlier January-June figure of 3.2 Mt of semis exports, up 18% year on year with June at a record 695,000 tonnes, is the wider context and is unchanged.

Dated reporting of 07-September-2026 has Iran saying an agreement with Oman to manage Strait of Hormuz shipping is days away, after more than three weeks of talks covering proposed inbound and outbound routes, the security and sovereignty of both states, and a proposed joint coordination centre; a separate 26-August report states a temporary maritime route had already been agreed. THE WATERWAY HAS NOT REOPENED: full reopening is reported as conditional on the United States fulfilling commitments under a June interim deal that has since lapsed, and no agreement is signed. THE ESCALATION FACTS ARE NOT DELETED - Iran said it attacked ten ships near the Strait and the United States said it sank five Iranian tankers. WHAT HAS CHANGED IS EVIDENTIAL CATEGORY, FROM UNCONFIRMED RUMOUR TO DATED MULTI-OUTLET REPORTING, AND THAT IS WHY THE CORRIDOR IS RE-RATED WHILE THE PHYSICAL POSITION IS NOT DECLARED REPAIRED. RE-RATED THIS RUN ON MATERIAL CHANGE. About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf production is exported through it. THE CORRIDOR RE-ESCALATED OVER THE WEEKEND after a week in which this page had carried a de-escalation: US strikes on two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on 30-August, Iranian retaliation against US bases, and an IRGC claim that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines. Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it. President Trump stated on 01-September that strikes would be limited and the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large oil volumes moving; both statements are dated and both are carried. THE PHYSICAL POSITION BEHIND THE HEADLINES IS THE PART THAT HAS NOT CHANGED: Qatalum remains at roughly 60% of its 648 kt nameplate on reduced gas with no published restart timetable and a second Hydro force majeure outstanding; Alba has reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March, 19% of 1,623 kt, with no announced restart and a stated intention to replace rather than restart them; EGA's Al Taweelah smelter is at 25% of cells with full production reaffirmed for Q1-2027. Gulf primary output ran roughly 40% below pre-war levels in April. This is the one corridor on the page where the disruption is both real and, in Qatalum's and Alba's cases, undated.

flows.note: REVISED THIS RUN ON NEW PUBLIC CUSTOMS DATA. China's AUGUST PRIMARY ALUMINIUM IMPORTS fell 14.65% year on year to 185,500 tonnes, up just 0.16% month on month, with RUSSIA SUPPLYING 178,150 TONNES OR 96% of the total; Australia contributed 2,920 tonnes, Indonesia 2,180 and Malaysia 1,800. Net imports were 163,600 tonnes, down 14.67% year on year but up 6.44% month on month. THE STATED CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL: domestic capacity at the 45-million-tonne policy ceiling, resilient end-use demand from power grid investment, electric vehicles and photovoltaic mounting structures, and inventory drawn down through extrusion exports rather than primary imports. The source is explicit that imports have not collapsed but maintained a steady inflow. THE CORRIDOR READ: China at the ceiling is importing less primary and exporting more semis, and 96% of what it does import comes from a single discounted-origin supplier. That combination reduces Chinese competition for ex-China primary units - which is a headwind for ex-China premiums and for the ex-China tightness case, whatever the cause. The earlier compositional point remains valid context: a high liquid-aluminium proportion means less deliverable ingot reaches the Chinese domestic market even at capped output.
